stem: A wage record for 40 workers gives cumulative counts at each upper class boundary. Up to Rs 10: 4 workers. Up to Rs 20: 12. Up to Rs 30: 25. Up to Rs 40: 36. Up to Rs 50: 40. How many workers earned wages in the class interval (30, 40]?

per_option_rationale.rationale: Frequency in (30, 40] = cumulative frequency at 40 minus cumulative frequency at 30 = 36 - 25 = 11.
The student reads the cumulative frequency at 30 as 26 instead of 25, giving 36 - 26 = 10. This is a one-unit arithmetic slip when reading the table.

The student reads off the cumulative frequency at the upper boundary 40, which is 36, and reports that as the frequency of the class rather than computing the difference. This treats cumulative frequency as class frequency.
The student subtracts the cumulative frequency at 20 from the one at 40, spanning two intervals: 36 - 12 = 24. This uses the wrong lower reference point in the ogive.

explanation: In a cumulative frequency table, a class frequency is the difference of two cumulative counts. Subtract the count at the lower boundary from the count at the upper boundary. For (30, 40]: cf(40) - cf(30) = 36 - 25 = 11.

explanation_sections.punchline: Class frequency is a difference of two cumulative counts, not the cumulative value itself. For (30, 40]: 36 - 25 = 11.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: this is a less-than ogive table. The decisive move is to locate the two consecutive cumulative values that bracket the target class. Subtract the smaller (at the lower boundary) from the larger (at the upper boundary). Never read off the upper cumulative count as the class frequency - that gives the cumulative total up to that point, not the class count. Recipe: (1) find cf at upper boundary of target class, (2) find cf at lower boundary, (3) subtract.
explanation_sections.lesson: A cumulative frequency at any boundary is a running total, not a class count. Every class frequency is recovered by one subtraction of two adjacent cumulative values. The trap in this item is option 3 (reading 36 directly), which reports the running total at 40, not the frequency inside (30, 40].
explanation_sections.timing: 75 seconds. Locate 25 and 36 in the table (15 seconds). Subtract to get 11 (5 seconds). Cross-check by verifying the other classes sum to 40 total if time allows.
